question.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-8{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -8 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get $3{x}_{1}=4{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{{x}_{3}}{3}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}7 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 25\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 25\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}25 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 25\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
